newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Clark hopes for coalition before APEC in Nov.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Clark hopes for coalition before APEC in Nov.

text.p: New Zealand Labour leader Helen Clark said on Thursday it was possible but "optimistic" that coalition negotiations could be completed in time for Labour's trade spokesman Mike Moore to attend an APEC ministerial meeting in Manila on November 22.

Asked if the talks could be completed in two and a half weeks in time to send Moore, Clark said: "It would be nice. I hope so. I think it is optimistic, but it would be wonderful if it could happen. I would very much like to have Mike Moore go to APEC. The normal course of events is for the prime minister to go and the minister of trade to be closely involved."
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum is to hold a leaders' meeting in the Philippines on November 25 after the ministerial meeting.

New Zealand now has a caretaker National Party government after an inconclusive general election on October 12. Nationalist New Zealand First, which holds the balance of power, is negotiating with both National and Labour on the possibility of forming a coalition with one or the other.
Clark said if a caretaker government was still in office it would be foolish to send representatives from both sides of the political spectrum to APEC.
"No I think that would be foolish. I think the question is if anyone goes at all," Clark told Reuters.
Labour entered its fourth round of negotiations with economic nationalist New Zealand First on Thursday.

Caretaker Prime Minister Jim Bolger, whose negotiating team met NZ First earlier on Thursday, told Reuters the need to determine who would attend the APEC summit did not put pressure on the coalition talks.
Asked when a decision would be made on who to send he said: "In sufficient time. It is not a problem."
